cat > /analysis-results/README.md << 'ENDREADME'
# cFlow Analysis Results for ImageMagick

## Tool
- **cFlow**: GNU cflow 1.7 (installed via apt-get)
- **Repository**: https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/cflow.git/

## Target Project
- **ImageMagick**: Cloned from https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick
- Source directories analyzed: MagickCore, MagickWand, coders, filters

## Analysis Files

### Forward Call Graph (GNU format)
- `cflow_magickcore_full.txt` - Full forward call graph for all MagickCore C source files (brief mode)
- `cflow_magickcore_core.txt` - Detailed forward call graph for 10 core MagickCore files
- `cflow_magickcore_part2.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 2
- `cflow_magickcore_part3.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 3
- `cflow_magickcore_part4.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 4
- `cflow_magickwand_all.txt` - Full forward call graph for all MagickWand C source files
- `cflow_magickwand.txt` - Forward call graph for key MagickWand files
- `cflow_coders_key.txt` - Forward call graph for key image format coders (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)
- `cflow_filters.txt` - Forward call graph for filter modules

### Reverse Call Graph (who calls each function)
- `cflow_magickcore_full_reverse.txt` - Reverse call graph for all MagickCore (brief mode)
- `cflow_magickwand_reverse.txt` - Reverse call graph for key MagickWand files

### Cross-Reference
- `cflow_magickcore_full_xref.txt` - Cross-reference listing for all MagickCore
- `cflow_magickcore_xref.txt` - Cross-reference listing for 10 core MagickCore files

### ASCII Tree Format
- `cflow_magickcore_full_tree.txt` - ASCII tree representation of call graph for all MagickCore

## cFlow Options Used
- Default (GNU format): Forward call tree starting from main/entry points
- `-r` / `--reverse`: Reverse call tree (shows callers instead of callees)
- `-x` / `--xref`: Cross-reference listing only
- `-T` / `--tree`: ASCII art tree output
- `-b` / `--brief`: Brief output
- `--no-main`: Show all functions, not only those reachable from main

## Summary
GNU cflow was used to analyze the control flow of the ImageMagick C source code.
The analysis covers:
1. **MagickCore** - The core image processing library (~80 C source files)
2. **MagickWand** - The MagickWand API layer (~21 C source files)
3. **Coders** - Image format codecs (key formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIFF, BMP, etc.)
4. **Filters** - Image filter modules

Each output file shows function call hierarchies, showing which functions call which,
enabling understanding of the code structure and call relationships across ImageMagick's
extensive C codebase.
ENDREADME

GNU cflow README
Copyright (C) 2005-2025 Sergey Poznyakoff
See the end of file for copying conditions.

* Introduction

This file contains brief information about configuring, and installing
GNU cflow. It is *not* intended as a replacement for the
documentation, instead it is provided as a brief reference only.
Please be sure to read the accompanuing documentation before using the
utility. See section `Documentation' below.

For the generic configuration options, see the file `INSTALL'.
Refer to file `ABOUT-NLS' for information regarding internationalization.

* History

The GNU cflow was initially written in 1997, when I needed a utility
that could display the control flow in a C program. The latest updates
in its old repo date back to 1999. Then, as I no longer needed the
package, it fell into oblivion.

Six years later a thread in gnu-devel mailing list had shown that
there is a kind of demand for that sort of utility, so I decided to
resurrect it and make a full-fledged package of it. On 2005-04-12 it
was dubbed a GNU package.

* Current Status

The package is fully operational. It compiles and runs on any
GNU/Linux and most decent UNIX-like systems. It supports all command
line switches required by POSIX, plus a number of extended ones. It is
able to produce output in two formats: in GNU cflow format (which is
the default) and in POSIX format.

Currently the utility is only able to process C sources. It is the
only deviation from POSIX specs, which requires ability to process
YACC and LEX sources as well as binary object files. This support will
appear in future versions.

Emacs module cflow-mode.el works with files in GNU cflow format (as
opposed to POSIX format). It has been tested with Emacs 24.2.1.

* Compilation

Please see the INSTALL file in this directory for the generic instructions
on how to use configure. There is currently only one package-specific
configuration option: --enable-debug, which compiles the package with
-g (or -ggdb if appropriate) option. Use it if you plan debugging
cflow.

See the end of file for copying conditions.

* Introduction

This file contains brief information about configuring, and installing
GNU cflow. It is *not* intended as a replacement for the
documentation, instead it is provided as a brief reference only.
Please be sure to read the accompanuing documentation before using the
utility. See section `Documentation' below.

For the generic configuration options, see the file `INSTALL'.
Refer to file `ABOUT-NLS' for information regarding internationalization.

* History

The GNU cflow was initially written in 1997, when I needed a utility
that could display the control flow in a C program. The latest updates
in its old repo date back to 1999. Then, as I no longer needed the
package, it fell into oblivion.

Six years later a thread in gnu-devel mailing list had shown that
there is a kind of demand for that sort of utility, so I decided to
resurrect it and make a full-fledged package of it. On 2005-04-12 it
was dubbed a GNU package.

* Current Status

The package is fully operational. It compiles and runs on any
GNU/Linux and most decent UNIX-like systems. It supports all command
line switches required by POSIX, plus a number of extended ones. It is
able to produce output in two formats: in GNU cflow format (which is
the default) and in POSIX format.

Currently the utility is only able to process C sources. It is the
only deviation from POSIX specs, which requires ability to process
YACC and LEX sources as well as binary object files. This support will
appear in future versions.

Emacs module cflow-mode.el works with files in GNU cflow format (as
opposed to POSIX format). It has been tested with Emacs 24.2.1.

* Compilation

Please see the INSTALL file in this directory for the generic instructions
on how to use configure. There is currently only one package-specific
configuration option: --enable-debug, which compiles the package with
-g (or -ggdb if appropriate) option. Use it if you plan debugging
cflow.

{"command": "cat > /analysis-results/README.md << 'ENDREADME'
# cFlow Analysis Results for ImageMagick

## Tool
- **cFlow**: GNU cflow 1.7 (installed via apt-get)
- **Repository**: https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/cflow.git/

## Target Project
- **ImageMagick**: Cloned from https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick
- Source directories analyzed: MagickCore, MagickWand, coders, filters

## Analysis Files

### Forward Call Graph (GNU format)
- `cflow_magickcore_full.txt` - Full forward call graph for all MagickCore C source files (brief mode)
- `cflow_magickcore_core.txt` - Detailed forward call graph for 10 core MagickCore files
- `cflow_magickcore_part2.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 2
- `cflow_magickcore_part3.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 3
- `cflow_magickcore_part4.txt` - Forward call graph for MagickCore files batch 4
- `cflow_magickwand_all.txt` - Full forward call graph for all MagickWand C source files
- `cflow_magickwand.txt` - Forward call graph for key MagickWand files
- `cflow_coders_key.txt` - Forward call graph for key image format coders (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)
- `cflow_filters.txt` - Forward call graph for filter modules

### Reverse Call Graph (who calls each function)
- `cflow_magickcore_full_reverse.txt` - Reverse call graph for all MagickCore (brief mode)
- `cflow_magickwand_reverse.txt` - Reverse call graph for key MagickWand files

### Cross-Reference
- `cflow_magickcore_full_xref.txt` - Cross-reference listing for all MagickCore
- `cflow_magickcore_xref.txt` - Cross-reference listing for 10 core MagickCore files

### ASCII Tree Format
- `cflow_magickcore_full_tree.txt` - ASCII tree representation of call graph for all MagickCore

## cFlow Options Used
- Default (GNU format): Forward call tree starting from main/entry points
- `-r` / `--reverse`: Reverse call tree (shows callers instead of callees)
- `-x` / `--xref`: Cross-reference listing only
- `-T` / `--tree`: ASCII art tree output
- `-b` / `--brief`: Brief output
- `--no-main`: Show all functions, not only those reachable from main

## Summary
GNU cflow was used to analyze the control flow of the ImageMagick C source code.
The analysis covers:
1. **MagickCore** - The core image processing library (~80 C source files)
2. **MagickWand** - The MagickWand API layer (~21 C source files)
3. **Coders** - Image format codecs (key formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIFF, BMP, etc.)
4. **Filters** - Image filter modules

Each output file shows function call hierarchies, showing which functions call which,
enabling understanding of the code structure and call relationships across ImageMagick's
extensive C codebase.
ENDREADME
echo "README created""}
